published.citation: Deming et al. 2023, dayside brightness temperature at 4.5 µm (uniform reanalysis of Spitzer's eclipses, CDS J/AJ/165/104 table 2): 1460 +/- 139 K, https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..104D/abstract

temperature.note: Its day side's brightness temperature is measured in secondary eclipse at 4.5 µm (Spitzer IRAC) and nobody has imaged it, so the color is a Planck spectrum at its published temperature.
temperature.chosen: 1 measured of 1 rows; the smallest relative uncertainty, then the longest wavelength
